verses.1: Paul, the apostle of Christ Jesus, by the will of God, and Timothy, brother in the church of God, who lived in Corinth. With all the saints who were present throughout the entire Age of Faith.
verses.2: May grace and peace be with you from our God the Father and from Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.3: Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of all prayers and God of all supplications.
verses.4: Please, help us in all our troubles. Help us to be able to ask those who are in distress for their help, through the prayer we offer to them.
verses.5: For just as Christ’s suffering is increased for us, so also is our own redemption through Christ increased.
verses.6: Whether we suffer, it is for your sake and for your salvation. Whether we pray, it is also for your sake, so that you may be able to endure their suffering with patience, just as we also suffer those sufferings.
verses.7: And our hope is indeed for your sake. You know that, as friends in times of trouble, we will also help each other out.
verses.8: We do not want to deceive you, brothers, about the sorrow we have suffered in Assyria. We have been overwhelmed by too much pressure, to the point that we were unable to continue living.
verses.9: But they themselves accepted the responsibility of responding to death. This was so that we might not deceive ourselves, but instead serve the God who raises the dead.
verses.10: He who has raised us from death and will also raise us again; to whom we have clung, and we will still cling.
verses.11: Together with your colleagues, they work hard for our benefit, so that the gift given to us from many people can be truly appreciated by all of us.
verses.12: For this is our glory: the testimony of our consciousness that we have been transformed in this world through the grace and sincerity of God, not through worldly wisdom, but through God’s gift. This is especially true regarding you.
verses.13: For we will not write anything else to you, but what you already know or can understand. I hope that by the end, you will truly understand it.
verses.14: Just as you also drove us away from various places, so too, our pride has been driven away by you. Just as you drove us away from those places on the day of our Lord Jesus.
verses.15: And with this belief in mind, I intended to come to you earlier, so that you could prepare for the second time.
verses.16: And to go through your land into Makedonia, and then again from Makedonia back to you, and to be sent to Judea through you.
verses.17: So, am I really using this opportunity for my own benefit? Or am I acting in a selfish manner, so that I can have Naí and Oú with me?
verses.18: But the Lord is true, and He knows that our words to you are not correct.
verses.19: For Jesus Christ, the son of God, who has been preached to you through us, by me and Silvanus and Timotheus, did not become a “Naï” or “Oo”. Instead, it was in him that this happened.
verses.20: For all the messages of God, in Him lies the Naí; and therefore, through Him, Amén also becomes known to God, through us.
verses.21: But you, surely, lead us along with you to Christ, and make us God’s people.
verses.22: He also sealed us and granted us the gift of marriage through the Spirit in our hearts.
verses.23: I, however, ask the Lord to be my witness that I will no longer go to Corinth, as I am afraid of you.
verses.24: Not only do we guide you in your faith, but we also become partners in your joy. For it is through faith that you have been united with us.
